title: What parts of this trailer would immediately tell you it was made by an AI-assisted solo developer?
author: Confident_Bass_474
selftext:
Genuine question.

I've been building a carp fishing game called Bankside and have partly relied on AI throughout development.

After looking at a project for so long it's hard to spot weaknesses objectively.

I'd love honest feedback on the trailer, especially anything that looks amateur, inconsistent, overly AI-generated or simply not ready for a Steam release. Please note that meshes will be upgraded before release.

https://reddit.com/link/1xxmmiy/video/6zidyw35iy1i1/player

comments.author: amunozo1
comments.body: The font. All AI slop games and webpages use the same fonts and visual style. Changing those will be crucial.

replies.author: Key_Actuary_3892
replies.body: To be clear - the font and font styling/gradient etc., not just the font itself. A good exercise would be scrolling some of the downvoted posts on this sub showing off their games and seeing if any of it looks similar to yours, as well as seeing what people hate about them from comments.

comments.author: tworc2
comments.body: Font, UI, syntax, grammar, the choice of words.

replies.author: Kepler___
replies.body: I think right now UI might be one of the loudest ones for me. AI makes what would have been considered pretty slop layouts even before it was a thing when you let it design. Makes sense in hindsight I guess. Most games that had a lot of effort put into them have pretty wildly different designs that are unique to the game. Might be hard to train that in the typical fashion.

comments.author: teejayaiartdirector
comments.body:
Looks like a lovely game to me, but I play around with AI a lot so I do spot stuff.

Is it Claude? (For me it got that Claude look to it), graphics are either procedural or blender? (may be procedural blender), game engine Unity or Godot (it's very difficult to spot if a game does not use a game engine).

comments.author: egonosz
comments.body: Colors in ui, dumb lines everywhere and the fonts, that is what Claude defaults to.

comments.author: Felmeric
comments.body:
All of the text reads like AI. It uses that weird stilted wording: "Some fish take a lifetime" what does that even mean? Who talks like that? AI talks like that. "A camp that grows with you" is another AI line. Old Tom's dialog seems like something AI would write. "Seasons follow the real calendar" is a line from a feature list that your AI inserted verbatim into the trailer. 

The large "nine waters" line looks like the title drop when it's actually just more AI writing describing how many maps there are. That's another thing that's obviously AI, that constant over explaining thing it does. AI can't see, so the idea of "show don't tell" doesn't make sense to it. AI constantly wants to add text explaining what is going on, on screen or why the thing it is showing is happening. 

Your characters are obviously made by AI. They have that look like they came out of a CAD program instead of a 3d modeling program. 

It looks like it could be a fun fishing game but this trailer looks like AI made everything involved. I know the trailer was the hardest part for me too so I hope you take this as a list of things to improve on and not an attack on your efforts.

comments.author: MadCat0911
comments.body:
Font, UI, Color pallete of the sunset for sure, the way the person looks, text wording. 

At this point it might be better to ask what doesn't look like Claude made the decisions here and you just said ok.

comments.author: Crafty-Following8762
comments.body:
This… instantly knew that Claude made it. It is especially glaring this text design is so ill-suited to this kind of game. It looks like it belongs to a fantasy RPG, not a cozy game with simple low poly graphics. Choose a sans-serif font. Something playful. Do away with those accent under and over lines Claude put on there. It is too much.

The UI is obvious, too. Again, it doesn’t match the game. Look at other games for references — cozy games and children’s games, and try to create something with a similar feeling. It’ll do a lot to create the right atmosphere.

It looks like a fine game. Everything else looks perfectly okay. If you just changed the graphic design, it wouldn’t look like an “AI game”, it’d just look like an indie game.

comments.author: TheAuthorBTLG_
comments.body: Claude does two bad things. First, it uses phrases like “item verb” as if an inactive item was a human. Nobody talks like that. Also, it uses default fonts without any special treatment, so it looks low-budget.

replies.author: KhaosPT
replies.body:
Ohhh interesting

Edit: the item verb. It drives me nuts when I just need some quip and it generates a weird sentence

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: I feel like 2 is one of the most overlooked things in ai game dev that I should write a post about it.

comments.author: quadtodfodder
comments.body: Little bits of stuff floating around in the air everywhere seems to be AI shorthand for "quality game', but I'll be hecked in the bim bim if I understand why.

comments.author: mugsy342
comments.body: I agree with the UI/font as everyone else here, I'd also personally say the transition from first person to the wider top down view gives two contrasting ideas of visual presentation. Thats not necessarily a problem, but I would work more towards that and other transitions, and how you pace, and it should line up with how fluid or not fluid it is in game. If the camera is panning smoothly in and out of first person between mechanics, Id argue seeing that exaggerated here would be smart, and the opposite applies as well, albeit you'd need to be a little more creative potentially. No idea if others would agree, but it feels like that could help the contrast not be as stark

comments.author: ThePunisher2072
comments.body:
EVERYTHING. Just everything. If you’ve worked with Claude you recognise every single aspect of it:

The font  
The layout of the texts  
The synthesizer sounds with melodic tones to emulate other sounds  
The ultra basic environment models without textures  
The primitive shapes based characters without textures  
The music  
The trees. They’re always the same kind of trees.  
The color palette with sunny sunlight

comments.author: quadtodfodder
comments.body:
4 is kind of a big deal: AAA special effects, but rudimentary graphics/finish elsewhere is a top AI tell.  

Also the 122% polish level on the UI is weird.  Is this Knights' Gold of the RealmDragons' Outing XXIV?  No it is a fishing game.  So why is the font made of gold?

comments.author: Soggy_Macaroon3148
comments.body: Overall color Ballance and patchworky ragged character details are blatant ai

replies.author: Luciferrrro
replies.body:
Yep its hard to maintain color balance as there are like 100 different locations and 100 playable characters and 500 monsters.

For patchworky ragged character details everything is based on their lore - which is based on our (my and my friends custom world developed for over 25 years of tabletop DND sessions.

We had a very interesting world so few years ago in 2018 i decided to develop a game similar to Darkest Dungeon - my motivation was to learn frontend dev and React that was getting popular - i was backend dev back then. So base of engine code and architecture is very old, ofc refactored like 10x over the years and AI helped a lot to increase performance and add new systems. Architecture as fine from begining as i was always into gamedev, but only as a hobby. As a proffesional im tech lead and i know all arch/code patterns. Game dev has its specific patterns but they are very similar, things like composition, events based state, state-animations patterns, For years the game was simple React froms/cards with only text descriptions, and played by me and my friends (it has single player and local network PVP multiplayer where you can use singleplayer developed characters).   
  
I slightly abandoned it for 2-3 years, but with AI getting better i decided to rework it and add visual layer  
  
how it looked back then:  
 

https://i.redd.it/cjwb3wcuqc2i1.png

It is from first rework with first Chat GPT in 2022 anyway, for older screenshots i must search my old PC.
